messages:
sarah_pm: Quick sync — Customer BetaCorp is asking for a tenant-level retention exception: keep user request traces + short-term audit logs for 18 months instead of our default 6 months. They cite retained-evidence requirements for a regulated pilot. Need an agreed request flow + acceptance criteria. Who owns the runbook?

aj_eng: What exactly is in scope? request traces vs full audit log? sizes? is this read-only retention or an export? :eyes:

kelly_cs: BetaCorp specifically called out: request tracing, prompt/responses (non-PII subset), and auth events. Estimate: ~120GB/month. They want SLA for export on legal hold. Urgent — asking for timeline by EOW.

michael_compliance: Heads-up: 18 months is doable but increases SOC2/ISO evidence surface. We need: (1) documented approval trail, (2) access controls + encryption posture, (3) export process for legal holds, and (4) periodic attestation. Also flag: retention exceptions must not undermine our default audit sampling for controls evidence.

tess_legal: Legal wants a mandatory legal-hold overlap check. If a legal hold occurs during the exception window, we must freeze and produce a snapshot within the hold SLA. Also need justification template and an owner.

ryan_ops: Ops shout — storage and index cost will spike. Proposal: create a retention-exception object with TTL, owner, justification, and an optional snapshot/export hook. Exception entries are soft-state until approved, then enacted by retention-service. Need revocation path.

sarah_pm: Proposed flow: 1) CS files request via /exceptions UI or API with justification + contract reference, 2) Compliance and Legal triage (48h), 3) Engineering scope estimate + runbook (72h), 4) Ops cost signoff, 5) Exec/Security approval for >12mo, 6) Rollout + monitoring + attestation. Acceptance criteria (draft): - approval ticket exists in JIRA/reference, - encrypted-at-rest with tenant BYOK check (if customer requires), - oncall runbook for export and freeze, - retrospective cost estimate in billing, - automated audit trail for who approved and when.

aj_eng: Implementation notes: minimal API prototype for review:
```
POST /v1/retention-exceptions
{
  "tenant_id": "T-123",
  "scope": ["request_traces","auth_events"],
  "duration_months": 18,
  "justification": "BetaCorp regulated pilot",
  "requester": "kelly_cs",
  "contract_ref": "CON-2026-001"
}
```
On approve, retention-service should create a snapshot id and a policy entry with a revocation timestamp. We also need an automated billing tag.

michael_compliance: Add to acceptance: periodic attestation every 6 months, and an automated alert 30 days before expiration to re-request or revoke. Also require a 'least-privilege' ACL for retained artifacts.

tess_legal: Add legal template for justification and a checkbox: "I confirm no conflicting litigation hold" — if checked is false, route to legal immediately.

ryan_ops: Oncall runbook (short): - How to produce export snapshot: `curl https://ops-api/exports?snapshot_id=...` - Who to page: eng-oncall + compliance lead - Storage restore steps and retention override revert. We should add an automated playbook in PagerDuty.

kelly_cs: BetaCorp will accept a gated 2-week pilot if we can provide the runbook and contract amendment. They also want an ability to request emergency snapshots during the pilot.

sarah_pm: Decision requests: - Approve flow above as MVP? - Add requirement: security signoff for >12mo? - Owner for runbook (ops or eng?) Suggest ops own runbook, eng owns enforcement. Approve to move to RFC? :thumbsup: / :thumbsdown:

aj_eng: +1 to ops owning runbook. Engineering will own retention-service and API. Suggest we ship a minimal enforcement mode: flagged exceptions get retained but marked with an internal billing tag and audit metadata.

michael_compliance: +1, but require compliance audit flag and attestation schedule in RFC.

tess_legal: +1 from legal on the flow, subject to the justification template. I'll draft language.

deploy-bot: retention-service v2.3.1 deployed to staging at 1970012355 — integration tests passed.

sarah_pm: OK — I'll open an RFC and assign owners: ops -> ryan_ops for runbook, eng -> aj_eng for API, compliance -> michael_compliance for attestation cadence, legal -> tess_legal for templates, cs -> kelly_cs for customer comms. Target: RFC + prototype by next Wed. Thanks everyone.
